headline: Antonelli comes out on top after 4 lead changes in Spa-Francorchamps
standfirst: Kimi Antonelli won the Belgian Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 1.952s ahead of Charles Leclerc, with Max Verstappen completing the podium after 45 laps of Spa-Francorchamps.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: Kimi Antonelli lined up first on the grid. Antonelli converted that into the lead at the end of lap one. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Hadjar, up 5 places to 16th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 4 times. Laps led: Antonelli (29), Leclerc (13) and Norris (2). Antonelli took the lead for good on lap 34. The race was neutralised by 1 safety car period (lap 1–4).

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Antonelli made 1 stop, running medium → hard → soft tyres. The field made 28 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.3s for Leclerc on lap 20. 9 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Isack Hadjar made up the most ground, climbing 15 places from 21st to 6th. Timing recorded 214 on-track position changes, 22 of them by Hadjar.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Perez (lap 14), Stroll (lap 26) and Russell (lap 1) failed to finish.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 28°C to 34°C, with air at 17–19°C. Lando Norris set the fastest lap, a 1:48.890 on lap 44.
